parsed.explanation: Combined regime imposes birth-sex facilities criminally, including private businesses in this division up to one year, with a documented arrest and 24-hour men's-ward hold elsewhere under a similar law. National entry rules allow refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for document discrepancy, X markers are no longer issued, and custody reports include hormone removal, forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. Courts and suits offer partial recourse and several orders are enjoined, but no working remedy neutralises the operative bathroom, document and custody exposures. No execution pathway is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport X/mismatched markers no longer processed; consular cable requires refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and some waivers exist. Litigation challenges passport policy.
entry_documents.interaction: Division retains X on state ID, diverging from passport, increasing mismatch at hotels, police checks and facilities.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections model includes hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. Bathroom arrest elsewhere resulted in men's-ward hold.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime and employment rulings exist; courts have enjoined some orders, but custody policies remain documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can lead to refusal/fraud inquiry; arrest for facilities can lead to birth-sex custody placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded facilities matching identity. Division law effective July 2026 criminalises restroom/changing-room use not matching birth sex in government and public-facing private businesses, up to one year for first offence.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Suit filed April 2026 on due-process, equal-protection and privacy grounds; narrower trespass statute elsewhere requires willful entry plus refusal to depart. No enforcement under division law yet identified.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal binary definition reinforces division ban; private-business reach removes even private-sector refuge.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors banned in many states; proposed national rules would bar public insurance under 18; DOJ subpoenaed hospitals for minors' records. Division hospital facilities covered by bathroom ban.
care_services.protection: Emergency care not documented as barred; adult care protections not documented in dossier.
care_services.interaction: Care seeker or minor can be exposed through records, disclosure rules and facility bans.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders frame gender ideology, direct investigation/prosecution over social transition of minors, military and sports bans; 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; diversity materials removed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Some orders blocked/enjoined; civil-liberties suits active; 2022 marriage-recognition statute and 2020 employment ruling remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing legitimises birth-sex enforcement at borders, schools, facilities and custody.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division requires schools, childcare and medical professionals to disclose minor's trans status to parents within three days; teacher pronoun law; national order directs criminal prosecution for facilitating social transition. Blocked 2022 felony parental-travel bill is not operative.
minors_guardians.protection: 2022 bill that would have imposed felony/life liability for taking child out of state for care was blocked; parental permission routes remain for some care.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling guardian/minor faces disclosure, school, care and facility exposure distinct from adult visitor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 66% poll support for birth-sex document laws indicates hostile public climate; allied governments issued advisories; no division-specific trans violence above general homicide rate documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 23 states have state bias laws; police response to trans victims not documented in division.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostile climate plus criminal bathroom law increases police-call and confrontation risk when outed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport, executive-order and bathroom challenges unresolved; whether June 2026 narrowing remains in force and suit outcome unknown; offence classification discrepancy unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts, legal aid FAQ, civil-liberties litigation and some injunctions documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists but is slow and has not prevented Supreme Court allowing passport restriction or division law taking effect.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: birth-sex institutional placement with assault risk, criminalised gendered-space use, short jail exposure and weak practical remedy. This case adds private-business criminalisation and national custody abuse reports, but retains functioning courts and no capital pathway.

Lower: 0.35 involves hours-long detention, fines and exclusion without imprisonment. Here first-offence bathroom use carries up to one year, arrest/ward hold is documented under comparable law, and entry can trigger lifetime-ineligibility inquiry.

Much lower: 0.55 involves ward assignment by document marker with delayed care and ethics remedies, no criminal penalty for identity. Here facility mismatch is criminalised across public and private businesses, with custody harm documented nationally.

parsed.synthesis: Operative interaction is document/binary definition -> entry refusal or fraud inquiry -> birth-sex facilities criminalised even in private businesses -> arrest and birth-sex custody, with documented custody abuse nationally. Courts provide real but slow and incomplete recourse, and no execution is documented, preventing a near-zero score. The universal, criminalised facility rule and severe custody reports place the combined regime in High Risk, materially below administrative-friction anchors.
